change.title: pr-2
change.description: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: Reloading or re-opening the unsubscribe link mutes the topic
findings.body:
The action flips the level on every GET. Above `regular` it goes to `regular`. At `regular` or below it goes to `muted`. The first visit takes a tracking/watching user to `regular`. A page refresh, a Back/Forward navigation that reloads the page, a second click on the email link, or a mail client or link scanner that prefetches the URL sends them to `muted`. The user sees no error, and the page text still says only that notifications will stop. A user who only asked to stop emails can end up with the topic muted. Make the action idempotent: set a fixed target level, for example `regular` when above `regular` and otherwise leave it unchanged. Alternatively, make the change a POST triggered by a confirmation button.

The action also changes state on a GET, so any prefetch triggers it.

findings.title: `tu` can be nil (or have a nil level), causing a 500 on the unsubscribe link
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no `topic_users` row for the topic. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError at line 107. The notification email can be sent without a row, for example when the user's notification comes from a category or tag watch rather than a topic-level setting. I did not confirm every path that sends mail without a row. `TopicUser.change` and `TopicUser.create_lookup` in `app/models/topic_user.rb` handle a missing row, so the code base expects it. Handle nil by treating the level as the default (`regular`) and creating the row. `TopicUser.change` creates the row if missing.

findings.title: `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`
findings.body: The UI path for changing notification state is `TopicUser.change(user_id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`. It is used, for example, at `app/models/topic.rb:725` for pin clearing. In `app/models/topic_user.rb`, `change` publishes the `notification_level_change` message on `/topic/:id` (lines 112-114) and sets the reason fields. A plain `save!` does neither. Other open tabs on the topic therefore keep showing the old level. `notifications_reason_id` stays at its old value, for example the "you are watching because you replied" reason. The new route hides the reason text only on this page. Consider using `TopicUser.change`.

findings.title: No tests for the new `unsubscribe` action, `Topic#unsubscribe_url` or the email link
findings.body: The PR adds a state-changing endpoint and a redirect branch (slug mismatch or missing slug). None of them is tested. The branches that need coverage are the redirect, tracking/watching to regular, regular to muted, a missing TopicUser row, and a logged-out user. `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` only passes the new `unsubscribe_url` argument and asserts nothing about it. Nothing checks that the rendered email body or html part contains the per-topic link. Add controller specs and an assertion on `unsubscribe_link` output.

findings.title: Typo `stopNotificiationsText`
findings.body: The property name is misspelled (`Notificiations`). The same misspelling is in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3`. Rename it in both places. The file also lacks a trailing semicolon after `})`.

findings.title: Client route does not unsubscribe; text is misleading on in-app navigation
findings.body: The unsubscribe happens only in the server `topics#unsubscribe` action, on a full page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`. This route only fetches `/t/:id.json` and renders "You will stop receiving notifications". Navigating to that URL within the Ember app, for example through a pushState transition, shows the message but changes nothing. The route should not be reachable except through the server render. Consider making the page reflect the actual state, or have the route perform the change explicitly.

findings.title: Whitespace-only reformatting unrelated to the feature
findings.body: The changes in `app/models/topic_user.rb`, `app/views/email/notification.html.erb`, `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, `app/mailers/user_notifications.rb` and `topic-from-params.js.es6` are style-only (hash braces, var to const, indentation, `if` modifiers). They make the diff harder to review and add merge-conflict risk. Consider dropping them from this PR.

findings.title: Unrelated routing change: `post_number` constraint removed from summary routes
findings.body: The `summary` routes lose their `post_number: /\d+/` constraint (lines 439 and 442). The routes have no `:post_number` segment, so the constraint was inert and removal is probably harmless. It is unrelated to unsubscribe and not mentioned in the PR body. Confirm it is intentional or revert it.

contracts.action: User opens the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email (GET /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe)
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing path that changes notification level is TopicsController#set_notifications / TopicUser.change (publishes MessageBus and sets the reason). The new action does not use it.
contracts.before_after: Before: no per-topic unsubscribe. After: the action loads the TopicView, redirects to the slugged URL on slug mismatch (before any state change), then flips the TopicUser level with a plain save! (above regular goes to regular, otherwise muted) and renders show.
contracts.visible_effect: The Ember route /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe loads the topic JSON through GET /t/:id.json. It shows 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>' plus the notifications button with the new level and no reason text (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:12-15).
contracts.failure_mode: The action runs once per GET, so a reload or prefetch moves regular to muted silently. A missing TopicUser row raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500. A logged-out user is sent through ensure_logged_in.

contracts.action: Email now carries a per-topic unsubscribe link
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing 'unsubscribe_link' i18n string in lib/email/message_builder.rb (html_part line 67, body line 90) interpolates template_args.
contracts.before_after: Before: unsubscribe_link only had user_preferences_url. After: it also needs %{unsubscribe_url}. Only UserNotifications passes add_unsubscribe_link: true with unsubscribe_url. RejectionMailer reserves add_unsubscribe_link, so no other caller hits a missing interpolation argument. Topic#unsubscribe_url is built from Topic#url, which is absolute (Discourse.base_url).
contracts.visible_effect: The HTML and text emails show a second paragraph 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here'.
contracts.failure_mode: A new caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url would raise a missing interpolation argument.

contracts.action: Client unsubscribe page rendering: fancyTitle is interpolated into i18n text and output with triple-stash
contracts.equivalent_path: Other templates that render {{{model.fancyTitle}}}, for example topic.hbs:38.
contracts.before_after: The same fancy_title server value is used and rendered unescaped, as in topic.hbs.
contracts.visible_effect: The title shows in bold inside the sentence.
contracts.failure_mode: The server pre-escapes fancy_title, so no new injection is seen. A failed topic load rejects the route model promise and the standard error route shows.

summary: The per-topic unsubscribe feature is wired end to end: the email link, the route, the server action and the Ember page. The server action has two defects. The state change is not idempotent, so a reload, Back or a link prefetch moves a topic from regular to muted silently. And a missing TopicUser row crashes it with a 500. It also bypasses TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus update goes out and the notification reason stays stale. The new endpoint has no tests, and the PR carries unrelated whitespace and routing churn. I did not run any code.
